title: Logged model tags: set_logged_model_tags writes through _bulk_upsert with last-value-wins dedupe by tag key
answers: Setting or updating tags on a logged model is slow or makes many SQL round-trips when a call has many tags
Why does a logged model tag write fail on PostgreSQL with CardinalityViolation when the same tag key is repeated in one call?
Where is logged model tag upsert handled, and how does it behave per database dialect?
body:
Path: Logged model tag writes (set_logged_model_tags, a batch of LoggedModelTag key/value pairs for one model_id) pass through mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore.set_logged_model_tags, which resolves the model's experiment_id and then hands the rows to _bulk_upsert on SqlLoggedModelTag.
Rule: Dedupe the incoming tags into a dict keyed by tag.key (last value wins) before building the row dicts, then call _bulk_upsert once. This replaces the per-tag session.merge loop, which issued one SELECT and one INSERT/UPDATE per tag. On SQLite and PostgreSQL _bulk_upsert emits INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (model_id, tag_key) DO UPDATE, on MySQL INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, in batches of 100; other dialects (MSSQL) fall back to a session.merge loop.
Symptom: On PostgreSQL, a call that repeated a tag key (for example two LoggedModelTag entries with key 'dup') failed with CardinalityViolation ('ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time'). The old merge loop had silently kept the last value, so the same request succeeded on SQLite and MySQL.
Constraints: Applies to logged model tags only; the dedupe is needed because one ON CONFLICT statement cannot touch the same (model_id, tag_key) row twice. Empty tag lists pass an empty row list and are a no-op. delete_logged_model_tag is not changed. Regression coverage is test_set_logged_model_tags_bulk_upsert in tests/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store/test_sqlalchemy_store_runs.py, which includes a repeated-key case and a 150-tag batch crossing the 100-row chunk.
Applies: SQL tracking store logged model tag writes (set_logged_model_tags) on SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MSSQL.
applies: Logged model tag set/update in the SQL tracking store; not the run tag or file store paths.
says: Updating model tags fails with a database error when duplicate tag keys are provided.
Saving tags on a logged model is sluggish when applying a large tag batch.
Allow updating a model tag value multiple times within the same bulk save operation.
Applying metadata tags to a model crashes when duplicate keys exist in the request.
search: SqlAlchemyStore.set_logged_model_tags must deduplicate tag keys with last-value-wins before passing rows to _bulk_upsert. Without deduplication, PostgreSQL raised CardinalityViolation on ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE when a batch contained duplicate tag keys, whereas SQLite and MySQL previously hid the issue. This bulk upsert replaces the per-tag session.merge loop across SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MSSQL, applying exclusively to logged model tags.
